record_type: Historical source identity, reading observations and bounded retrieval coverage
question: What explains the decision to postpone AUTODIN II's transition to standard TCP/IP until after initial operational capability? Test cost, schedule, compatibility, technical readiness, and contractual commitments against the records.
principal_finding: The December 23, 1978 order asks DCA for a cost tradeoff analysis to determine transition timing; the analysis and reason for the April 3, 1980 after-IOC order remain unheld. Published TCP editions establish an evolving standard: February IEN 81 and August IEN 112 lack the later security/precedence sections, December IEN 124 announces their addition, and January 1980 IEN 129 / RFC 761 was ratified in April. This does not exclude interim working drafts, earlier TCP branches carrying related features, or existing IP support. Western Union revised both AUTODIN II host-protocol specifications on February 8, 1980; the THP reference page, dated February 21, 1979, cites the SRI and DCA family rather than a DoD standard protocol document. Neither sequence establishes the cause of deferral.

chronology.event: RATIFICATION AND DEFERRAL. Gerald P. Dinneen, now signing on Assistant Secretary of Defense (Communications, Command, Control and Intelligence) letterhead, approves the revised Management Plan, ratifies the DoD Standard TCP and IP specifications, makes their use mandatory for all packet-oriented DoD data networks with potential cross-boundary host-to-host connectivity, directs DCA to prepare workshop/seminars and implementation support documents, and states: 'The AUTODIN II implementation of these protocol standards will take place as soon after AUTODIN II IOC as possible.' The OSD Protocol Standards Working Group is disestablished and its responsibilities transferred to DCA panels. NO REASON IS STATED for the placement relative to IOC.

claim_table.claim: The December 1978 order itself names cost and schedule impacts on the AUTODIN II program as the consideration governing the transition's timing.
claim_table.basis: IEN 152 PDF p. 3, inspected: 'Recognizing that there may be cost and schedule impacts on the AUTODIN II program, the Defense Communications Agency should perform a cost tradeoff analysis to determine the optimum time for this transition.'
claim_table.limit: This states the anticipated grounds and frames timing as a variable to be optimized. It is not a finding about what the analysis concluded, and it precedes the analysis by four months.

claim_table.claim: The April 1980 memorandum defers AUTODIN II implementation to a point after IOC and gives no reason.
claim_table.basis: IEN 152 PDF p. 4, inspected: 'The AUTODIN II implementation of these protocol standards will take place as soon after AUTODIN II IOC as possible.'
claim_table.limit: The clause is a schedule placement with an urgency qualifier. The absence of a stated reason on the face of the order is not evidence that no reason was recorded elsewhere.

claim_table.claim: The DoD standard's own schedule slipped by roughly nine to twelve months against the December 1978 order, and the DoD security, compartmentation and precedence content entered the standard TCP specification only in December 1979.
claim_table.basis: IEN 152 PDF p. 3 (drafts January 1979, finals April 1979); IEN 81 of February 1979 whose preface has no such content; IEN 124 of December 1979 whose preface announces it; IEN 129 / RFC 761 of January 1980 repeating it; IEN 134 characterizing 123/124 and 128/129 as the first and second tries at the DoD Standard versions; IEN 145 recording the stamping. August 1979 IEN 112 was checked during validation and likewise lacks the later sections.
claim_table.limit: This dates published editions and ratification, not all working drafts or AUTODIN II system readiness. No recovered document connects the standardization sequence to DCA's timing decision; security/precedence features existed in earlier TCP branches and IP.

claim_table.claim: The contracted AUTODIN II specification baseline was current, actively revised, and unreconciled with the DoD standard at the decision point.
claim_table.basis: AD-A081757: coordinated Revision 2 of THP and Revision 3 of TCP both dated February 8, 1980 under DCA200-C-637; THP reference list at printed p. 4, unrevised since February 21, 1979, cites the July 1976 SRI specifications and the DCA System Performance Specification and no DoD standard document.
claim_table.limit: A reference list is not a statement of intent, and its non-revision may reflect nothing more than which pages the revision touched. This establishes the state of the baseline, not that the contract caused the deferral.

claim_table.claim: Cost was the operative reason for the deferral.
claim_table.basis: The order asks for a cost tradeoff analysis; the Task Force's retrospective account records growing projected costs.
claim_table.limit: No cost figure, analysis, or recommendation connecting cost to the April decision was recovered. The Task Force's cost account concerns the program in 1981-82, not the 1980 protocol decision.

claim_table.claim: Protection of the IOC milestone was the operative reason.
claim_table.basis: The December order expected operation during FY 1980; the April order ties implementation to IOC and says 'as soon after' as possible, which reads as sequencing behind a milestone rather than abandoning the requirement; the DSB later records a two-year program stretched to four and a half years and continuing delay.
claim_table.limit: No contemporaneous document states this. The reading of 'as soon after ... as possible' is an interpretation of a schedule clause. The DSB account is retrospective and program-wide.

claim_table.claim: Technical infeasibility of the upgrade explains the deferral.
claim_table.status: Not established; existing host implementations weigh against a blanket infeasibility claim.
claim_table.limit: These concern host implementations and the standard, not the Western Union switch, SIP, CCU/TAC firmware, or the security kernel. The SIP and backbone side was not examined in this pass.

claim_table.claim: Contractual commitment under DCA200-C-637 explains the deferral.
claim_table.basis: The CDRL B006 specification baseline was maintained on the divergent branch to February 8, 1980, monitored by DCA Code 450, two months before ratification.
claim_table.limit: No contract modification, engineering change proposal, cost proposal, or correspondence bearing on a protocol change was recovered. Contract activity establishes a commitment in force, not that it was the reason.

claim_table.basis: Divergence is established by the Western Union specifications and by the December 1978 finding of unsuitability.
claim_table.limit: Divergence is what the upgrade was ordered to fix. It is the problem, not an explanation of the timing chosen to fix it.

claim_table.claim: The July 1980 OSD review group explains the April 1980 decision.
claim_table.basis: AD-A127476 printed p. 3 dates the review group's establishment to July 1980.
claim_table.limit: It postdates the ratification by three months. No document connects it to earlier work. It remains a lead for whether the deferral was revisited later.

claim_table.basis: AD-A100788 is AFIT/GCS/EE/80D-9, James W. Healy and Denzel Henderson, Air Force Institute of Technology School of Engineering, December 1980, a backbone-network simulation thesis on switch control module routing and queueing.
claim_table.limit: A full-text search of the 417 KB OCR layer returns no occurrence of TCP, host-to-host, IOC, or protocol upgrade. Precedence appears only as a traffic category in the simulation.

readings.passage: AUTODIN II is expected to become operational during FY 1980, to provide common-user data communications service for DoD computer systems and permit a reduction in the number of specialized data networks.
readings.interpretation: Fixes the schedule expectation held at the moment of the upgrade order. AUTODIN II reached only a partial IOC in July 1981.

readings.passage: Because the host-to-host protocol being developed for AUTODIN II evolved from an early version of TCP and is unsuitable for internetwork operation, the AUTODIN II TCP will have to be upgraded to the standard protocol set. Recognizing that there may be cost and schedule impacts on the AUTODIN II program, the Defense Communications Agency should perform a cost tradeoff analysis to determine the optimum time for this transition. DCA should provide the results of this analysis by April 1979.
readings.interpretation: The order is for a cost tradeoff analysis to determine the optimum time, not for a cost/schedule analysis at large. The timing of the transition is treated as the open variable from the outset, and cost and schedule impacts on the AUTODIN II program are the named grounds.
readings.correction: Earlier records described this as 'a cost/schedule analysis'. The instrument the memorandum orders is a cost tradeoff analysis; cost and schedule impacts are the recognised concern that motivates it.

readings.passage: I am forming an OSD Protocol Standards Working Group chaired by the Director, Information Systems. I ask each addressee to nominate a representative. Names should be provided by 8 January 1979 to LTC Wilcox (695-3287). ... Draft specifications for these protocols will be available in January 1979. Final specifications should be distributed by April 1979 following review by the working group and testing by DCA and DARPA. At that time, I expect to promulgate these standards and set dates for their adoption.
readings.interpretation: Establishes the intended standardization schedule against which the actual January 1980 specifications and April 1980 promulgation can be measured. Also names the working group and its point of contact as retrieval handles.

Records the April 1980 ratification and assignment of continuing responsibilities. The working group was ordered formed in December 1978; the phrase about work during the past year does not reset its formation date.
readings.observation: The memorandum is on Assistant Secretary of Defense (Communications, Command, Control and Intelligence) letterhead, dated 3 APR 1980, and carries a handwritten signature that appears identical to the December 1978 signature of Gerald P. Dinneen. No typed name block is present on this page; the typed 'Gerald P. Dinneen, Principal Deputy' visible in the image is reversed show-through from PDF p. 3. Treat the identification as apparent from the signature, not as printed attribution.

readings.passage: Hosts are connected to the SCMs via a Segment Interface Protocol (SIP), and must have the standard Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) to pass useful traffic to other hosts.
readings.interpretation: Read in context this is the AUTODIN II standard TCP; section VIII.5 speaks of 'the standard specification required of AUTODIN II subscribers'. The paper uses 'standard TCP' for both families, which is exactly the ambiguity the brief warns about.

readings.passage: the WIN (WWMCCS Intercomputer Network) and the SACDIN (Strategic Air Command Digital Network) are examples of AUTODIN II subnetworks, and their computers will join the network as hosts sharing in their own special communities of interest. They will use the AUTODIN II standard SIP and will also be required to use the DoD standard TCP unless they can obtain a waiver from this requirement based on the lack of need to communicate with others beyond their own subnet community of interest.

To achieve this desired interoperability, it is required that the subscribers of internetted systems use a common standard TCP and Internet Protocol (IP). DoD policy has recently been stated which requires DoD data network subscribers having requirements for interoperability to adhere to these standards. What remains is for the gateways themselves to be developed and implemented. A research and development program to develop the gateways is now underway under the aegis of Rome Air Development Center.
readings.limit: This is an open-literature architecture paper, not a decision record, and it is silent on AUTODIN II's own protocol transition.

readings.passage: subject to the provision that these subscribers use appropriate standard TCP and IP protocols and that the gateways between the relevant networks are implemented.
readings.interpretation: Repeats the same pairing of standards adherence with gateway availability.

readings.interpretation: The January 1980 standard carries the same preface sentence as the December 1979 IEN 124, with the edition count advanced from seven to eight. readings.passage: It should be easy to interface higher level protocols like the ARPANET Telnet or AUTODIN II THP to the TCP.
readings.interpretation: The ratified standard still names the AUTODIN II THP as an intended higher-level protocol, consistent with the accommodation pattern already recorded in the brief for RFC 791.

readings.passage: This document describes the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). There have been five previous editions of the TCP specification ...

local.scope: Recorded capture, not distributed: spec-63a13b54-autodin 2 sip ADA071670.txt, the OCR extract of the March 1979 AUTODIN II Segment Interface Protocol specification, AD-A071670. 263608 bytes; md5 a85417b9736f667e24c12323d3a80a46; sha256 d2936e5ef1efc5e6b2d34ee9ea1b1708da042969c12c66d51b450ae19cf34a15.
local.performed: 2026-09-13, as a bounded recordkeeping correction after the first pass. The first pass did not search this extract for transition terms and the omission was not recorded.
local.outcome: No relevant hit. The DoD-standard term family, including the bare strings DOD and 'Department of Defense', and the standardization and interoperability families, and 'upgrad' in any form, do not occur anywhere in the extract. 'Transition' occurs at eleven lines, and every occurrence is a protocol state-machine transition: the prescribed state transition stimuli and responses of section 3, coupled SIP and Mode VI transitions between Interface Down and deeper states, and the state transition charts listing next states and resulting outputs. None refers to a transition to a DoD standard protocol or to a program schedule.
local.collateral_reading: The extract's thirteen TCP occurrences are all the SIP header's TCP Version No. field and its explanatory text: the field identifies the originating SIP user, 'TCP is one' and 'the code for no TCP is zero', and is used to identify the proper user of SIP. This is a version-identification field within the AUTODIN II SIP, not a provision for adopting a different protocol. It is recorded as a reading of the extract, not as evidence about the deferral.
local.consequence: The SIP specification as extracted contributes nothing to the deferral question. This is a bounded negative about one OCR extract of one specification. It is not a reading of the original scan, and OCR loss could in principle hide a term; the decisive passages of this document were not re-inspected as images in this correction.

corrections_to_existing_records: The December 1978 memorandum orders a 'cost tradeoff analysis to determine the optimum time for this transition', not a 'cost/schedule analysis'. Cost and schedule impacts on the AUTODIN II program are the recognised concern that motivates it. Earlier brief wording conflated the two.

The April 3, 1980 memorandum carries a signature apparently identical to Gerald P. Dinneen's on the December 1978 memorandum, on ASD(C3I) letterhead. The covering note to IEN 152 describes the two memoranda as coming from different offices. Record the office change, and note that PDF p. 4 carries no typed name block.
The National Security Archive Western Union TCP scan has a DTIC identity, AD-A081756, and a same-day companion, AD-A081757, the THP Revision 2. The Western Union comparison section should carry both.

The DoD requirements named in the December 1978 order entered the standard TCP text in the December 1979 edition (IEN 124), not in the January 1980 edition. January 1980 is the second try and the ratified text.
